figures.observed_content: Generic increasing concave-down curve with two points; horizontal Δx and vertical Δy.
figures.technical_interpretation_and_conditions: Represents a finite difference quotient. The derivative limit requires a base point held fixed and differentiability there.

figures.observed_content: Satellite and observer above/on curved Earth; s is satellite altitude, h the slant distance, L the red surface arc.
figures.technical_interpretation_and_conditions: The curved geometry gives context only. Earth radius and a governing spherical equation are absent.

figures.observed_content: Flat-Earth right triangle: vertical leg s, hypotenuse h, horizontal leg L.
figures.technical_interpretation_and_conditions: For fixed s, h²=s²+L²; take L≥0 and h≥s. Do not identify this straight L with an exact spherical arc length.

figures.observed_content: Left line ends with filled point at (0,0); right line starts with open point at (0,1).
figures.technical_interpretation_and_conditions: Matches f(x)=−x for x≤0 and x+1 for x>0, not the printed second condition x≥0.

figures.observed_content: Continuous-looking oscillating curve interrupted by one open circle.
figures.technical_interpretation_and_conditions: Schematic removable hole; no axes, coordinate or alternative filled value specified.

figures.observed_content: Two horizontal levels separated at x0; both endpoints are hollow.
figures.technical_interpretation_and_conditions: Illustrates unequal finite one-sided limits. The value at x0 is unspecified and cannot remove the jump.

figures.observed_content: Reciprocal hyperbola in quadrants I and III, asymptotic to both axes.
figures.technical_interpretation_and_conditions: Correct 1/x geometry on x≠0; +∞ from right and −∞ from left at zero.

figures.observed_content: Positive-side oscillations of persistent amplitude become increasingly rapid near the vertical axis.
figures.technical_interpretation_and_conditions: No analytic formula or scale is supplied. Only the right-side behavior is pictured; oscillation alone is not enough unless its amplitude fails to vanish.

figures.observed_content: Top: reciprocal branches with red tangent samples. Bottom: negative derivative branches with corresponding red samples.
figures.technical_interpretation_and_conditions: Correct qualitative f=1/x and f′=−1/x² for x≠0; both branches of f decrease; derivative is even and negative.

figures.observed_content: Parabolic arc passes above a rectangular building; caption y=400−16t², −5≤t≤5.
figures.technical_interpretation_and_conditions: Schematic physical scene. Axes, units, horizontal-motion model and building height are not specified.

figures.observed_content: Top: downward parabola with positive, zero and negative tangent samples. Bottom: decreasing red line through origin with corresponding samples.
figures.technical_interpretation_and_conditions: Consistent with y′=−32t. Closed derivative endpoints imply an unstated extension or one-sided convention.

figures.observed_content: Unit-radius circular arc, positive acute θ, vertical sinθ segment and arc labelled θ.
figures.technical_interpretation_and_conditions: Arc length equals θ only with unit radius and radians; drawn lengths use θ>0.

figures.observed_content: Small-angle enlargement retaining radius 1, sinθ vertical segment and arc θ.
figures.technical_interpretation_and_conditions: Qualitative comparison supporting the sine ratio; does not itself supply a squeeze proof.

figures.observed_content: Unit sector with horizontal projection cosθ and residual horizontal gap 1−cosθ; arc θ.
figures.technical_interpretation_and_conditions: Labels consistent for the pictured positive acute angle. Arc length differs from vertical displacement sinθ.

figures.observed_content: Small-angle sector with near-horizontal radius and short horizontal gap 1−cosθ.
figures.technical_interpretation_and_conditions: Qualitative scale comparison; needs a bound to establish the quotient limit and a sign/symmetry step for negative angles.

claims.source_claim: Δy/Δx tends to dy/dx as Δx→0.
conditions: Δy=f(x0+Δx)−f(x0), base x0 fixed.
Δx≠0 while taking the limit.
A finite derivative must exist.
claims.independent_check: This is the defining difference-quotient limit.

claims.source_claim: dq/dt is current; ds/dt is speed; dT/dx is temperature gradient.
conditions: q denotes charge transferred; s denotes distance traveled, not signed position.
Temperature varies along the indicated spatial coordinate.
claims.independent_check: If s meant signed position, its derivative would be velocity rather than speed.

claims.source_claim: ΔL/Δh measures sensitivity of inferred position to range error.
conditions: The geometric relation and other parameters must be held fixed.
A derivative describes the local small-error limit, not an exact arbitrary finite-error ratio.
claims.independent_check: Figure 3 yields L=√(h²−s²) and dL/dh=h/√(h²−s²) for fixed s and h>s; these formulas are reviewer deductions, not printed equations.

claims.source_claim: lim as x→3 of (x²+x)/(x+1) equals 3.
conditions: Denominator at 3 equals 4.
claims.independent_check: Direct substitution gives 12/4=3; algebraic cancellation gives x on x≠−1.

claims.source_claim: The displayed derivative difference quotient excludes a zero denominator.
conditions: Set Δx=x−x0 to interpret its printed x→x0 limit; otherwise use Δx→0.
claims.independent_check: A limit uses punctured inputs; substituting Δx=0 into the original quotient is undefined.

claims.source_claim: Continuity at x0 means lim f(x)=f(x0).
conditions: f(x0) is defined and finite.
For the pictured interior-point setting the finite two-sided limit exists.
At a domain endpoint the appropriate relative/one-sided interpretation applies.
claims.independent_check: This separates existence of a nearby limit from the assigned function value.

claims.source_claim: Printed piecewise f: x+1 for x>0; −x for x≥0.
conditions: Second branch must be x≤0 to match Figure 4 and the following page.
claims.independent_check: As printed, x>0 receives two conflicting values and x<0 receives none. Corrected limits at zero: left 0, right 1; f(0)=0.

claims.source_claim: For x>0 the displayed lim as x→0 of f(x) is 1; f(0)=0 and f is continuous from the left only.
conditions: Use corrected piecewise function from C07.
The limit value 1 is the right-hand limit; the unrestricted two-sided limit does not exist.
claims.independent_check: Write x→0+ for the displayed limit to preserve the prose restriction.

claims.source_claim: Right limit uses x→x0+ and x>x0; left uses x→x0− and x<x0.
claims.independent_check: These definitions are correctly printed here and contradict the reversed pairing on the next page.

claims.source_claim: A removable discontinuity has equal one-sided limits but a different or undefined point value.
conditions: The common one-sided limit must exist as a finite real number.
An undefined point value alone is not sufficient.
claims.independent_check: For sin x/x at zero, the later limit is 1, so assigning that value removes the hole.

claims.source_claim: Jump discontinuity: both one-sided limits exist but differ.
conditions: Both limits are finite.
The x<x0 limit uses x0− and the x>x0 limit uses x0+.
claims.independent_check: The source sentence reverses both superscripts; the graph correctly depicts unequal limiting levels.

claims.source_claim: 1/x→+∞ from the right of 0 and →−∞ from the left.
conditions: Infinity notation denotes unbounded divergence, not a finite real limit.
claims.independent_check: There is no two-sided finite or common signed-infinite limit at zero.

claims.source_claim: The illustrated oscillatory function has no limit at the origin.
conditions: Oscillations retain distinct limiting heights arbitrarily near zero.
No specific analytic function is printed.
claims.independent_check: The displayed right-side nonconvergence is enough to preclude a two-sided limit. Oscillation with shrinking amplitude can instead have a limit.

claims.source_claim: For f(x)=1/x, f′(x)=−1/x².
claims.independent_check: Direct quotient simplifies to −1/[x(x+h)] for h≠0, x+h≠0 and tends to −1/x².

claims.source_claim: The derivative of an odd function is even, and vice versa.
conditions: Domain symmetric under x↦−x.
Function differentiable at the paired points.
Vice versa means the derivative of an even function is odd.
claims.independent_check: From parity and difference quotients: odd f gives f′(−x)=f′(x); even f gives f′(−x)=−f′(x). The inference f′ even ⇒ f odd is false, e.g. f=x+1.

claims.source_claim: y(t)=400−16t² on −5≤t≤5, paired with a straight decreasing derivative graph.
conditions: Ordinary two-sided derivative on −5<t<5; endpoints need one-sided derivatives or polynomial extension.
Negative t uses a time origin before which the pumpkin is rising; the apex occurs at t=0.
Units are not stated on this page.
claims.independent_check: y′=−32t; heights at −5,0,5 are 0,400,0; derivative values under the extension are 160,0,−160. The derivative is signed vertical velocity, not speed.

claims.source_claim: lim sinθ/θ=1 as θ→0 with θ in radians.
conditions: θ≠0 within quotient.
Geometry shown uses 0<θ<π/2.
Negative side follows because sinθ/θ is even.
claims.independent_check: Sector/triangle areas give sinθ≤θ≤tanθ, hence cosθ≤sinθ/θ≤1; geometric continuity of cosine at 0 or the bound 1−cosθ≤θ²/2 completes the squeeze. These quantitative steps are absent from the printed visual argument.

claims.source_claim: lim (1−cosθ)/θ=0 as θ→0.
conditions: Negative-angle handling is not represented by unsigned lengths in the drawings.
claims.independent_check: For real radian θ, |sin(θ/2)|≤|θ|/2 gives 0≤1−cosθ≤θ²/2 and |(1−cosθ)/θ|≤|θ|/2→0. This is an independent check, not a printed proof.

claims.source_claim: The short segment 1−cosθ becomes much smaller than the “vertical distance θ along the arc.”
conditions: The figure uses positive acute θ.
claims.independent_check: θ is the unit-circle arc length, not the vertical displacement. The latter is sinθ. Merely restating relative smallness gives no quantitative proof of the quotient limit.

claims.source_claim: Differentiability at x0 implies continuity at x0.
conditions: f(x0) is defined.
Derivative exists as a finite real limit under the ordinary definition.
Identity and quotient are used only for x≠x0.
claims.independent_check: f(x)−f(x0)=[(f(x)−f(x0))/(x−x0)](x−x0)→f′(x0)·0=0. Thus lim f(x)=f(x0). No substantive error found.

technical_findings.source_observation: Second branch is printed −x for x≥0.
technical_findings.basis: Graph has negative-x branch and filled origin; PDF5 states f(0)=0 and left continuity. Printed branches overlap incompatibly for x>0.

technical_findings.source_observation: The x<x0 clause carries x→x0+; the x>x0 clause carries x→x0−.
technical_findings.correct_statement_or_interpretation: Use x→x0− for x<x0 and x→x0+ for x>x0.
technical_findings.basis: Definitions on PDF5 are correct; signs on PDF6 are reversed. The worded jump criterion remains correct.

technical_findings.source_observation: θ is called a vertical distance along the arc.
technical_findings.correct_statement_or_interpretation: θ is arc length in the positive-angle unit-circle picture; vertical displacement is sinθ.
technical_findings.basis: The arc and the vertical segment are distinct geometric objects.

locator.detail: opening continuation of the piecewise example

technical_findings.source_observation: Displayed limit x→0 equals 1, with x>0 stated only in prose.
technical_findings.correct_statement_or_interpretation: It is lim x→0+ f(x)=1. The two-sided limit does not exist.
technical_findings.basis: Corrected example has unequal limits 0 and 1.

technical_findings.source_observation: Finiteness of the equal one-sided limits is not explicit; the undefined-value alternative can be misread.
technical_findings.correct_statement_or_interpretation: Both side limits must equal the same finite real L, and f(x0) must be absent or unequal to L.
technical_findings.basis: Undefined value alone does not imply removability; an infinite common limit cannot be repaired by a finite point value.

technical_findings.source_observation: Limit subscript is x→x0 while quotient is written with Δx.
technical_findings.correct_statement_or_interpretation: Read with the implicit relation Δx=x−x0, or write Δx→0.
technical_findings.basis: No calculation is wrong if the relation is supplied.

locator.detail: geometric proof statement and closing sentence

technical_findings.source_observation: The asserted sine-ratio proof rests on how the picture looks for small positive θ.
technical_findings.correct_statement_or_interpretation: A quantitative bound such as cosθ≤sinθ/θ≤1 plus cosθ→1 and an evenness step establishes the two-sided limit.
technical_findings.basis: The stated limit is correct; the bound and negative-side extension are not printed.

technical_findings.source_observation: “Gets much smaller” asserts the desired relative-size conclusion without establishing it.
technical_findings.correct_statement_or_interpretation: The bound |(1−cosθ)/θ|≤|θ|/2 for nonzero radian θ proves the conclusion on both sides.
technical_findings.basis: Follows from 1−cosθ=2sin²(θ/2) and |sin u|≤|u|; these quantitative steps are absent.

technical_findings.source_observation: “And vice versa” can denote two different logical statements.
technical_findings.correct_statement_or_interpretation: Valid intended meaning: even differentiable f has odd f′ on a symmetric domain.
technical_findings.basis: The converse f′ even ⇒ f odd fails for f(x)=x+1; source omits differentiability and symmetry conditions.

technical_findings.source_observation: Derivative endpoints are drawn closed although the given time interval is closed; negative time and units are unexplained.
technical_findings.correct_statement_or_interpretation: On the restricted domain, the usual two-sided derivative has −5<t<5; endpoint derivative values use an extension/one-sided convention. Time zero is at the apex. Units remain unspecified.
technical_findings.basis: The polynomial and qualitative derivative sketch are otherwise consistent.
